mainTopic: Young כהנים (רובים and פרחי כהונה), the guard posts of the כהנים and לויים in the בית המקדש, and using בגדי כהונה while sleeping
overview: The גמרא first explains why our משנה calls the young guards in בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ 'רובים' but the young כהנים in בית המוקד 'פרחי כהונה'. The רובים are too young to serve, while the פרחי כהונה are old enough. Next it quotes the משנה in מדות: the כהנים guarded the בית המקדש in 3 places and the לויים in 21. A פסוק in דברי הימים is brought as the source, but it adds up to 24 guards. The גמרא answers either by taking away 3 or by saying the 24 include the 3 posts of the כהנים, who are sometimes called לויים. It explains why the corner guards stand inside the הר הבית but outside the עזרה: a tired guard must be allowed to sit, and no one may sit in the עזרה except the kings of בית דוד. It also settles whether the עזרה had five or seven gates, with answers from אביי and רבא. Finally, it discusses whether the משנה about not sleeping in בגדי כהונה proves that a כהן may benefit from them. It concludes that the garments were placed next to the head, not under it, and רב פפא learns from this that תפילין may lie beside a sleeper's head.

steps.title: End of the question: why the name 'young men of the priesthood'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its question: why does our משנה use the name פרחי כהונה here, when earlier it said רובים?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Why does our משנה call them] 'young men of the priesthood'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last word of a question that started just before. The גמרא wants to know why the משנה uses two different names for the young כהנים, and it is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in our own משנה, the young guards in בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ are called רובים. Later in the same משנה, the young כהנים who sleep in בית המוקד are called פרחי כהונה. The question is whether the different names point to a real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'blossoms' of the priesthood: young כהנים

phrases.english: "Young men of the priesthood"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question that began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה use two different names (רובים and פרחי כהונה) for young כהנים?

steps.title: The two names describe two different age groups
steps.stepSummary: Yes, there is a difference. רובים are too young to do the עבודה, and פרחי כהונה are old enough to do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Yes. There, where they have not yet reached the age to do the עבודה, they are called 'רובים'. Here, where they have reached the age to do the עבודה, they are called 'פרחי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two names really do mean two different groups of young כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guards in בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ were young boys who could not serve yet, so they are called רובים. The כהנים sleeping in בית המוקד were getting ready for the morning עבודה, so they had to be old enough to serve, and they are called פרחי כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Young boys, below the age of serving
The service in the בית המקדש
There (the earlier line about בית אבטינס and בית הניצוץ) / here (the line about בית המוקד)

steps.whatToRemember: רובים are too young to do the עבודה. פרחי כהונה are young but already able to do it.

phrases.english: They say: Yes,
there, where they have not reached the age to do the service,
he calls them "young boys";
here, where they have reached the age to do the service,
he calls them "young men".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The names show age: רובים cannot yet serve, פרחי כהונה can.

steps.title: The כהנים guarded the בית המקדש in three places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in מדות: the כהנים kept watch in בית אבטינס, בית הניצוץ, and בית המוקד.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: In three places the כהנים keep watch in the בית המקדש: in בית אבטינס, in בית הניצוץ, and in בית המוקד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from מדות about guard duty in the בית המקדש. This sets up the list of the לויים and the question that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first part lists only the three posts of the כהנים. The לויים' posts come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The chamber of the אבטינס family, who prepared the קטורת
The Chamber of the Hearth, where the כהנים slept

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה in מסכת מדות.

phrases.english: In three places the priests keep watch
in the Temple:
in the Chamber of Avtinas, and in the Chamber of the Spark,
and in the Chamber of the Hearth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: guard posts in the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים guard in three places: בית אבטינס, בית הניצוץ, בית המוקד.

steps.title: The לויים guarded in twenty-one places
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: the לויים kept watch in 21 places, at the gates and corners of the הר הבית and the עזרה, and in three special spots.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the לויים in 21 places: five at the five gates of the הר הבית; four at its four corners on the inside; five at the five gates of the עזרה; four at its four corners on the outside; one in לשכת הקרבן, one in לשכת הפרוכת, and one behind בית הכפורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists all 21 guard posts of the לויים. This list is what the גמרא will ask about next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Add them up: 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 21. The posts are arranged in rings around the הר הבית and the עזרה, plus three single posts at special places.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple Mount, the outer area
The Temple courtyard, the inner area
The chamber where the פרוכת was woven
The קודש הקדשים, where the ארון and its cover stood

steps.whatToRemember: כהנים guarded 3 places; לויים guarded 21 places.

phrases.english: And the Levites in twenty-one places:

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה – עַל חֲמִשָּׁה שַׁעֲרֵי הַר הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: five at the five gates of the Temple Mount;
four at its four corners on the inside;
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the הר הבית, so these guards stood inside its outer wall.

phrases.english: five at the five gates of the courtyard;
and four at its four corners on the outside;
phrases.notes: Here 'its' means the עזרה, so these guards stood outside the courtyard wall.

phrases.english: one in the Chamber of the Offering,
and one in the Chamber of the Curtain,
and one behind the Chamber of the Ark Cover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה, moving from the כהנים to the לויים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לויים guard in 21 places: gates and corners of the הר הבית and עזרה, plus three special posts.

steps.title: Where do we learn the guard posts of the לויים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the לויים' guard posts.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these things learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the guarding of the לויים. This sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave a list without a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that the לויים guarded in these places.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things learned? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the list in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that teaches the guard posts of the לויים.

steps.title: The source is a פסוק in דברי הימים about the gatekeepers
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מסורא (or a ברייתא) brings the פסוק listing how many לויים stood on each side: six east, four north, four south, and more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה מסורא said, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: As it is written: 'Eastward were six לויים, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the אספים two and two; for the פרבר westward, four at the path, and two at the פרבר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that lists the guard posts of the לויים by direction, as the source for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the gatekeepers that דוד assigned for the future בית המקדש. Each direction gets a set number of לויים. The גמרא is also unsure who said this: רב יהודה מסורא or a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה
Storehouses (a place named in the פסוק)
An area on the west side named in the פסוק

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda of Sura said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:
As it is written: "Eastward were six Levites,
northward four a day,
southward four a day,
and for the Asuppim two and two.
For the Parbar westward, four
at the causeway, and two at the Parbar."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִסּוּרָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דברי הימים א 26:17-18 listing the לויים gatekeepers by direction.

steps.title: The verse counts 24 posts, not 21
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים point out that the פסוק lists 24 guard posts, while the משנה says the לויים guarded in only 21 places.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: But these add up to twenty-four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source it just brought. When you add up the guards in the פסוק, you get 24, not the 21 the משנה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק was supposed to prove the משנה's number of 21 guard posts for the לויים. Adding up the פסוק gives 24 instead. A source that gives a different number does not seem to prove the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: they are / they add up to

steps.confusionAlert: The 24 comes from counting every number in the פסוק: six east, four north, four south, "two two" (four) at the אספים, four at the road, and two at the פרבר.

phrases.english: They say: But these are twenty-four!
phrases.notes: "These" means the guards listed in the פסוק from step 6 (דברי הימים א 26:17-18).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source brought in step 6 because its count does not match the משנה in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק is the source for the 21 guard posts of the לויים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Numbers mismatch: the פסוק adds up to 24 and the משנה says 21.

steps.title: Only two guards at the אספים
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the doubled word "two two" at the אספים really means just two guards.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what the פסוק means: at the אספים there were two.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins to answer the question. He reads the doubled "two two" at the אספים as just two guards, not four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "two two" meant four guards, the total comes to 24. If it means only two, the total drops by two, to 22. This brings the count closer to 21 but does not reach it yet.

keyTerms.meaning: the storehouses (a place in the מקדש that had guards)

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
For the storehouses – two (two).
phrases.notes: The פסוק says "two two," but אביי counts only two guards here. Some versions leave out the second "two" in round brackets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7 by re-reading one part of the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Two two" at the אספים means four guards.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Two two" means only two guards, so the total drops to 22.

steps.title: Still 22, not 21
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that even after אביי's answer, the count is 22, still one too many.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, they are twenty-two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first answer. Taking away two guards from 24 still leaves 22, not 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reading fixed part of the problem. There is still one extra guard that does not fit the משנה's count of 21.

phrases.english: Still, they are twenty-two!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 8 only partly solves the problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After removing two guards, the total is 22, which is still more than 21.

steps.title: The second guard at the פרבר was just company
steps.stepSummary: The פרבר really had one guard. The second לוי only sat with him for company, because the spot was far outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The guard at the פרבר was really one person. The other one just went and sat with him to keep him company, because that spot was out on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the leftover problem. One of the two people listed at the פרבר was not a real guard post, just company for the guard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists two people at the פרבר, but only one of them was an official guard. The second sat there because the place was lonely and far out. That removes one more post and brings the count to exactly 21.

keyTerms.meaning: an outer area on the west side of the מקדש

steps.whatToRemember: 24 in the פסוק, minus 2 (the אספים are only two), minus 1 (the second person at the פרבר was just company) = 21 guard posts for the לויים.

phrases.english: That one of the Parbar – it was one,
and the other one, it was for company
that he went and sat beside him –
because it stood on the outside.
phrases.notes: "It" is the פרבר, which was out on the edge, so a guard there would be alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 and completes the count of 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the case: one of the people listed was not a real guard post
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both people at the פרבר were official guards.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one was a guard; the other sat with him for company, so the total is 21.

steps.title: What does the word פרבר mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word "לפרבר" in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "to the Parbar" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops briefly to ask what the strange word פרבר means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side question about a word, not a challenge. It fits here because the answer just said the פרבר was "on the outside."

keyTerms.meaning: what is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is "to the Parbar"?
phrases.notes: The word comes from דברי הימים א 26:18.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side question about a word used in the answer in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word פרבר.

steps.title: פרבר means "toward the outside"
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב שילא explains that פרבר is like saying "כלפי בר", toward the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב שילא said: It is like someone saying "toward the outside."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב שילא explains the word. פרבר sounds like "כלפי בר," which means "toward the outside."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name of the place describes where it was: out on the outer side. This matches step 10, which said the guard there needed company because the spot was on the outside.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Sheila said:
Like one who says "toward the outside."
phrases.notes: בר is Aramaic for "outside," so פרבר sounds like a short way of saying "facing out."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב שֵׁילָא: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר כְּלַפֵּי בַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרבר means "כלפי בר," toward the outside.

steps.title: All 24 are real: 3 for the כהנים and 21 for the לויים
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: read the פסוק as it is written, with 24 posts. Three belong to the כהנים and twenty-one to the לויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: there really are twenty-four, just as it is written. Three of them are the כהנים' posts and twenty-one are the לויים' posts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question from step 7 and gives a completely different answer. There is no need to remove anyone from the count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of re-reading words in the פסוק, this answer says the 24 includes the three guard posts of the כהנים from the משנה in step 3. Three plus twenty-one equals twenty-four, so the פסוק and the משנה match exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to match the פסוק to the משנה: (1) take away 3 to get 21 (אביי removes two at the אספים, and the גמרא then removes one at the פרבר); (2) keep all 24, with 3 for the כהנים and 21 for the לויים.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually there are twenty-four, as it is written.
Three of them – are of the priests,
phrases.notes: These are the three places from step 3: בית אבטינס, בית הניצוץ, and בית המוקד.

phrases.english: and twenty-one – are of the Levites.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה, כְּדִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question in step 7 and offers a different answer from אביי's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different answer: the count includes the כהנים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All 24 posts in the פסוק belong to the לויים, so the number does not match 21.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 24 posts include 3 for the כהנים and 21 for the לויים, which matches the משנה exactly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer uses the פסוק as the source for both the כהנים' posts and the לויים' posts in the משנה, without changing how any word is read.

steps.title: But the פסוק calls all the guards לויים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer that three posts belonged to כהנים, since the פסוק calls all the guards לויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here the פסוק writes 'לויים'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer, that three of the 24 posts were guarded by כהנים. The פסוק seems to say that all the guards were לויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 read the פסוק as 24 posts and split them: 3 for כהנים and 21 for לויים. But the פסוק itself calls the guards 'לויים'. So how can some of them be כהנים?

keyTerms.meaning: Levites, from the tribe of לוי

phrases.english: But here,
it is 'Levites' that is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 3 of the 24 posts belonged to כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls all the guards לויים, so it seems none of them were כהנים.

steps.title: כהנים are sometimes called לויים
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי יהושע בן לוי, there are 24 places where the תנ״ך calls כהנים 'לויים'. So the word 'לויים' can include כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: In twenty-four places כהנים are called לויים, and this is one of them: 'And the כהנים, the לויים, the sons of צדוק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'לויים' does not always mean regular לויים only. It brings רבי יהושע בן לוי, who showed that the תנ״ך often calls כהנים 'לויים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים also come from the tribe of לוי, so the תנ״ך sometimes calls them 'לויים'. The פסוק in יחזקאל is one example. That means the guard-post פסוק can include the three כהנים posts, even though it says 'לויים'.

keyTerms.meaning: the sons of צדוק, a family of כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Every כהן is also from the tribe of לוי. So calling a כהן a 'לוי' is not a mistake. It is just naming his tribe.

phrases.english: It is in line with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
In twenty-four places
priests are called Levites,
and this is one of them:
"And the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לויים' in the פסוק means only regular לויים, so no כהנים guarded.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לויים' can include כהנים, so the 3 כהנים posts fit the פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: The 24 guard posts are 3 for כהנים and 21 for לויים. The פסוק says 'לויים' because כהנים are also called לויים in many places.

steps.title: Where the guard posts stood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list. There were five posts at the gates of the הר הבית and four at its corners from inside. There were five posts at the gates of the עזרה and four at its corners from outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five on the five gates of the הר הבית, and four on its four corners from inside. Five on the five gates of the עזרה, and four on its four corners from outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that lists where the לויים stood guard. It is setting up the next question about 'inside' and 'outside'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two areas follow the same pattern of five gates and four corners. There is one difference: the corner guards of the הר הבית stand inside its wall, while the corner guards of the עזרה stand outside its wall. The next step asks about this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: the Temple Mount, the large outer area
the Temple courtyard, the inner holier area

phrases.aramaic: חֲמִשָּׁה – עַל חֲמִשָּׁה שַׁעֲרֵי הַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: Five: on the five gates of the Temple Mount,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מדות listing the guard posts.

phrases.english: and four: on its four corners, from inside.
Five: on the five gates of the courtyard,
and four: on its four corners, from outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה – עַל חֲמִשָּׁה שַׁעֲרֵי הַר הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who guarded to where the posts were
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הר הבית corner posts were inside its wall. The עזרה corner posts were outside its wall.

steps.title: Why inside for one and outside for the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the הר הבית guards stand inside while the עזרה guards stand outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the הר הבית, that we guard it from inside, and what is different about the עזרה, that we guard it from outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference it just quoted from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both areas are guarded in the same way otherwise. So we would expect the corner guards to stand in the same place for both. The גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

phrases.english: What is different about the Temple Mount
that we do it from inside,
and what is different about the courtyard
that we do it from outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הַר הַבַּיִת דְּעָבְדִינַן מִתּוֹכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the detail in Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the corner guards stand inside the הר הבית but outside the עזרה

steps.title: A tired guard must be able to sit
steps.stepSummary: A guard may sit on the הר הבית, so he stands inside it. No one may sit in the עזרה except the kings of בית דוד, so the guard stands outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: On the הר הבית, if a guard gets tired and wants to sit, he may sit, so we say inside. In the עזרה, if he gets tired and wants to sit, he cannot, because the Master said that sitting in the עזרה is allowed only for kings of בית דוד. So we say outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the guards' placement depends on whether they are allowed to sit down there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Guards stand for long hours and may need to rest. Sitting is allowed on the הר הבית, so its guards can stand inside. Sitting is not allowed in the עזרה, except for kings of בית דוד, so its guards stand outside where they may sit.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no sitting in the עזרה
the kings of the house of דוד

steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the general rule that no one may sit in the עזרה, which shows how holy that area is.

phrases.english: They say: The Temple Mount,
where if he gets tired and wants to sit, he may sit,
phrases.notes: תָּמַהּ usually means 'is amazed', but here it means the guard is worn out.

phrases.english: we say: from inside.
The courtyard, where if he gets tired and wants to sit,
he cannot sit,
as the Master said: There is no sitting in the courtyard
except for the kings of the house of David alone,
we say: from outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הַר הַבַּיִת, דְּאִי תָּמַהּ וּבָעֵי מֵיתַב – יָתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The guards are placed where they are allowed to sit if they get tired. That is inside the הר הבית, but outside the עזרה.
steps.whatToRemember: The guards stand where a tired guard is allowed to sit. That means inside the הר הבית and outside the עזרה, because only kings of בית דוד may sit in the עזרה.

steps.title: Did the עזרה have five gates or seven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'five gates of the עזרה' and challenges it from another משנה, which says the עזרה had seven gates.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Five on the five gates of the עזרה. Did the עזרה really have only five gates? But there is a contradiction: there were seven gates in the עזרה, three in the north, three in the south, and one in the east!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one line of the משנה and points out that another משנה gives a different number of gates for the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה speaks of five gates of the עזרה, each with a guard. Another משנה says the עזרה had seven gates. The two numbers seem to contradict each other, and the answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: חֲמִשָּׁה עַל חֲמִשָּׁה שַׁעֲרֵי עֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: The Master said: Five on the five gates of the courtyard.
Were there only five gates in the courtyard?!
But a contradiction was raised: There were seven gates in the courtyard,
phrases.notes: This is another משנה in מדות.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלֹשָׁה בַּצָּפוֹן, וּשְׁלֹשָׁה בַּדָּרוֹם, וְאֶחָד בַּמִּזְרָח!
phrases.english: three in the north, three in the south, and one in the east!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חֲמִשָּׁה עַל חֲמִשָּׁה שַׁעֲרֵי עֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a detail in Step 16 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that the עזרה had five gates with guards
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה says the עזרה had seven gates (3 north, 3 south, 1 east), so 'five' seems wrong.

steps.title: אביי: Two of the seven gates needed no guard
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the עזרה really had seven gates, but only five were guarded, because two of them did not need a guard.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Two of them did not need guarding.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from step 19 between 'five gates' and 'seven gates'. He says both are true: there were seven gates, but only five needed guards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is not counting every gate. It is only counting the gates that had a guard post. Two gates did not need a guard, so the guard list shows five even though there were seven gates.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Two of them do not need guarding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תְּרֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ לָא צְרִיכִי שִׁימּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different scope: the two משניות count different things (all gates vs. guarded gates)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות disagree about how many gates the עזרה had
steps.terutzMaskana: There were seven gates, and only five of them needed guard posts

steps.title: רבא: It is a disagreement between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: the two משניות really disagree, because different תנאים held different counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the contradiction. He says the two משניות simply follow different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי made the two משניות agree. רבא accepts that they argue: one תנא held five gates and another held seven. He will bring a proof right away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים (sages of the משנה era)

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a dispute between Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, different from אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disagreement between תנאים: the sources really argue
steps.terutzMaskana: The משניות follow different תנאים who argue about the number of gates

steps.title: Proof from the treasurers: Some held eight gates
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא. רבי נתן says there were thirteen treasurers to match thirteen gates. Take away the five gates of the הר הבית, and the עזרה has eight. So there are three opinions: eight, seven and five.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: One does not appoint fewer than thirteen treasurers and seven trustees. רבי נתן says: No fewer than thirteen treasurers, matching the thirteen gates. Take away the five of the הר הבית, and eight remain for the עזרה. So there is a תנא who says there were eight, a תנא who says seven, and a תנא who says there were five.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves that תנאים really argued about the number of gates. Using רבי נתן, he works out an opinion of eight gates for the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן says the thirteen treasurers matched thirteen gates in total. Our משנה gives the הר הבית five gates, so 13 minus 5 leaves 8 for the עזרה. Since one opinion says eight, it is clear that different תנאים gave different numbers. That supports רבא: five and seven are simply two of these opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Treasurers who looked after the money of the מקדש
Trustees, senior officers over the treasurers
One may not have fewer than

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the gates contradiction. אביי: seven gates, but only five were guarded. רבא: תנאים argued, with opinions of five, seven and eight.

phrases.english: As it is taught: One does not have fewer
than thirteen treasurers
and seven trustees.
Rabbi Natan says:
One does not have fewer than thirteen treasurers,
matching the thirteen gates.
Take away the five of the Temple Mount,
and eight remain for the courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא, אִיכָּא תַּנָּא דְּאָמַר תְּמָנְיָא הָווּ,
phrases.english: Evidently, there is a Tanna who says there were eight,
and there is a Tanna who says seven,
and there is a Tanna who says there were five.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר גִּזְבָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבא's claim that the matter is a disagreement between תנאים
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the number of gates was disputed by תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי נתן linking thirteen treasurers to thirteen gates, which leaves eight gates for the עזרה

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: They did not sleep in the holy garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה: the כהנים did not sleep in their holy garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: They would not sleep in the holy garments, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This quote sets up a question about using בגדי כהונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says the כהנים did not sleep in the garments. The גמרא will now ask what we can learn from the fact that it mentions only sleeping.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy garments the כהנים wore for the עבודה

phrases.english: They would not sleep
in the holy garments, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the משנה goes on. It continues: they took the garments off, folded them, and put them under their heads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after finishing the gates discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים did not sleep wearing the holy garments

steps.title: Walking is allowed, so one may benefit from priestly garments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reasons that only sleeping is forbidden, so walking in the garments must be allowed. That would show a כהן may get personal benefit from בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is sleeping that is not allowed, but walking, they may walk. Learn from this: priestly garments were given to be used for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה's wording. It says the garments may be used for personal benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה forbids only sleeping, then simply walking around in the garments, even outside the עבודה, seems allowed. Wearing them when not needed is personal benefit. So the גמרא wants to prove that בגדי כהונה may be used this way.

keyTerms.meaning: They were given to be used for benefit, so personal use is allowed

phrases.english: It is sleeping that is not allowed,
but walking, they may walk.
Learn from this:
priestly garments were given to be used for benefit!

steps.triggerLanguage: שֵׁינָה הוּא דְּלָא, אֲבָל הִילּוּךְ – מְהַלְּכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the exact wording of the משנה just quoted
steps.raayaObject: That a כהן may benefit from בגדי כהונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה forbids only sleeping, which suggests walking in them is allowed

steps.title: Walking is also forbidden; 'sleep' matches the next clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: walking is also forbidden. The משנה says 'sleep' only because its next clause talks about putting the garments under their heads while sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: The same is true that even walking is not allowed. The reason it teaches 'they would not sleep' is that it wants to teach the next clause: 'Rather, they take them off, fold them, and place them under their heads.' So it teaches the first clause too as 'they would not sleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 24. It explains why the משנה mentions sleeping even though walking is forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mention of sleeping is not meant to exclude walking. The משנה wants to describe what the כהנים did with the garments at bedtime, so it opens its rule with sleeping to fit that description. So no proof comes from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
The first part of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה mentions 'sleeping' only because of how it is worded, not to permit walking. Do not learn that walking in the garments is allowed.

phrases.english: They say:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ הִילּוּךְ נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: The same is true that even walking is also not allowed,
and the reason it teaches 'they would not sleep'
is because it wants to teach the later clause:
'Rather, they take them off and fold them'
'and place them under their heads,'

phrases.aramaic: קָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא נָמֵי: לֹא הָיוּ יְשֵׁנִים.
phrases.english: so it teaches the first clause too as 'they would not sleep.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ הִילּוּךְ נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof drawn in step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that walking in the garments is allowed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'sleep' was chosen to match the later clause about bedtime, not to exclude walking

steps.title: But placing them under their heads is itself a benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the later clause itself says the garments were put under their heads, like a pillow. That is personal benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this itself is difficult: 'And they place them under their heads.' Learn from this: priestly garments were given to be used for benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same problem from a new place: the very clause it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if walking is forbidden, using the garments as a pillow is clearly a personal benefit. So the משנה still seems to allow benefit from בגדי כהונה.

phrases.english: But this itself is difficult:
'And they place them under their heads.'
Learn from this
that priestly garments were given to be used for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the clause that step 25 relied on
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's words 'and they place them under their heads'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using the garments as a pillow is personal benefit, so the משנה seems to allow benefit from בגדי כהונה

steps.title: Read it as 'next to their heads'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means the garments were placed next to their heads, not under them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: next to their heads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the garments lay beside the head and were not used as a pillow, there is no personal benefit. So the משנה does not prove that one may benefit from בגדי כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: Say it instead as, read it as

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove that a כהן may benefit from בגדי כהונה. Walking in them is also forbidden, and they were placed next to the head, not used as a pillow.

phrases.english: Say: next to their heads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the words of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garments were used as a pillow under the head
steps.terutzMaskana: The garments were placed beside the head, so no benefit was taken

steps.title: רב פפא learns that תפילין may be placed beside one's head while sleeping
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא takes the answer that the garments were put 'next to' the head and learns from it that תפילין may also be put beside a sleeping person's head. We do not worry that he will roll onto them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We can learn from this that putting תפילין at the side of your head while sleeping is allowed. We do not worry that maybe you will roll over and land on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a practical הלכה from the answer in the last step: since the משנה lets the holy garments sit next to a sleeping כהן's head, תפילין may also sit next to a sleeping person's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said the garments were placed beside the כהנים' heads while they slept. One could worry that a sleeper will roll over and land on a holy object, which would be disrespectful. Since the משנה allowed the holy garments to be there anyway, רב פפא learns that this worry does not apply, and the same is true for תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: We can learn from this; a conclusion drawn from what was just said
Tefillin, the leather boxes with holy parchments
At the side, next to (the head)
We are not concerned; we do not worry about this risk

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה about how to treat תפילין at night, learned straight from how the משנה describes the בגדי כהונה in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Learn from this:
tefillin at the side [of one's head] are permitted,
and we are not concerned
that perhaps he will roll over and fall upon them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule about תפילין from the reading given in step 27, that the garments were placed beside the head.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may place תפילין beside his head while sleeping; we do not worry that he will roll onto them.

steps.title: Proof that 'next to their heads' is the right reading, because of כלאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the reading 'next to their heads.' If the garments were under the כהנים' heads, then even if personal benefit were allowed, it would still be forbidden because בגדי כהונה contain כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also makes sense that the משנה means 'next to their heads.' Because if you say it means 'under their heads,' then even if we grant that the כהנים may get benefit from the garments, it should still be forbidden because of the איסור of כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings logical support for the answer in step 27 that the garments were next to the heads: reading them as under the heads would cause a different problem, כלאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 24-26 discussed whether a כהן may get personal benefit from בגדי כהונה. Here the גמרא says that even if benefit were fine, lying on the garments would still be forbidden because they contain wool and linen together (כלאים). The Torah allows that mix only when it is worn for the עבודה, so the משנה must mean the garments were only beside the head.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is logical; this phrase introduces support for what was just said
They were given to be benefited from; personal benefit from them is allowed
Derive it instead from; there is another reason that already forbids it
Forbidden mixtures; here, wool and linen together (שעטנז)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה means the כהנים put their garments next to their heads, not under them. This both avoids the question of personal benefit and avoids the איסור of כלאים. From it רב פפא learns that תפילין may be put beside a sleeper's head.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems. 'Benefit' (steps 24-27) asks whether a כהן may use holy garments for himself. כלאים is a separate איסור about wool and linen, and it would forbid lying on them even if benefit were fine.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable
that [it means] next to their heads,
for if you say [it means] beneath their heads,
granted that they were given to be benefited from,
derive it [as forbidden] because of the prohibition of כלאים!
phrases.notes: בגדי כהונה have wool and linen mixed together. The Torah allows that only when the כהנים wear them for the עבודה, not for lying on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the answer in step 27 and backs it up with a separate reason, כלאים.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה means the garments were placed next to (כנגד) the כהנים' heads, not under them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The איסור of כלאים: the wool and linen in בגדי כהונה are allowed only when worn for the עבודה, so using them as a pillow would be forbidden even if personal benefit were allowed.
